'''Eloy Rodriguez''' (born January 7, 1947<ref name=CSY>{{cite web|url=http://csy.com/DrEloyRodriguez.htm |title=Profile at CSY.com |accessdate=2006-10-28 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20030408173505/http://csy.com/DrEloyRodriguez.htm |archivedate=April 8, 2003 }}</ref>) is an American [[biochemist]]. He is the James Perkins Professor of [[Environmental Studies]] at [[Cornell University]]. He was born in [[Edinburg, Texas|Edinburg]], [[Texas]].<ref name=ASCBprofile>{{Cite web |url=http://iweb.ascb.org/index.cfm?navid=90&id=503&tcode=nws3 |title=Profile at The American Society for Cell Biology |access-date=2006-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927001513/http://iweb.ascb.org/index.cfm?navid=90&id=503&tcode=nws3 |archive-date=2007-09-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His interest in medicine began with visits from the curanderos while sick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vaughn |first=Susan |date=2001-03-04 |title=Top Chemist Breaks Ground Inside and Outside the Lab |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-mar-04-wp-33118-story.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>    

Collaborating with [[primatologist]] [[Richard Wrangham]], Rodriguez introduced the concept of [[zoopharmacognosy]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Gerber |first=Suzanne |title=Not just monkeying around |date=November 1998 |journal=[[Vegetarian Times]] |issue=255 |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=https://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0820/is_n255/ai_21224859/print |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041029122245/http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0820/is_n255/ai_21224859/print |url-status=usurped |archive-date=October 29, 2004 }}</ref>

Rodriguez graduated from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in 1969 and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[phytochemistry]] and [[Botany|plant biology]] in 1975.<ref name=CornellArchive>[https://web.search.cornell.edu/search?q=cache:VsGir6R1luMJ:www.toxicology.cornell.edu/rodrig.htm+Eloy&access=p&output=xml_no_dtd&ie=UTF-8&client=default_frontend&proxystylesheet=default_frontend&oe=ISO-8859-1 Profile at Cornell's Toxicology website]{{dead link|date=October 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} (archived)</ref> Later, at the [[University of British Columbia]], he received medical postdoctoral training in [[medicinal botany]].<ref name=ASCBprofile /> He was an [[assistant professor]] of [[ecology]] and [[evolutionary biology]] at the [[University of California, Irvine]] from 1976 to 1994<ref name=CornellArchive /> before joining the faculty at Cornell.

Rodriguez contributed to the establishment of the disciplines of [[zoopharmacognosy]], and chemo-ornithology, which explores the [[chemical ecology]] of bird-insect-plant interactions.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Eloy Rodriguez {{!}} CALS |url=https://cals.cornell.edu/people/eloy-rodriguez |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=cals.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Rodriguez has mentored and trained hundreds of underrepresented minority and majority students in the sciences at Cornell University and the [[University of California, Irvine]], many of whom have gone on to careers in medicine, research, and environmental sciences.<ref name=":0" />

==Other interests==
Rodriguez, who is [[Mexican Americans|Mexican-American]], also serves as a faculty advisor for the Science Organization of Latinos at Cornell.<ref>[https://rso.cornell.edu/sol/members.php Members page for Cornell University Science Organization of Latinos] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061104184827/http://www.rso.cornell.edu/sol/members.php |date=2006-11-04 }}</ref> Cornell University currently has an award named after him called the "Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Conference Travel Award".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eloy Rodriguez Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion Conference Travel Award {{!}} CALS |url=https://cals.cornell.edu/school-integrative-plant-science/about/access-community-empowerment/eloy-rodriguez-diversity-equity-inclusion-conference-travel-award |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=cals.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref> 

Rodriguez is the director of the [[Cornell University Esbaran Amazon Field Laboratory]] located in the Amazon rainforest near [[Iquitos]], [[Peru]].

Rodriguez is the founder of the California Alliance for Minority Participation (CAMP) program funded by the National Science Foundation. As a result, the CAMP program spread from its home campus, University of California, Irvine, to the 9 other branches of the University of California.
